subject: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
question: Simplify √8 + √18, and rationalise the denominator of 2/(√3 − 1).
response_text:
$\sqrt{8} + \sqrt{18} = 2\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2} \approx 7.07$

$\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = \dfrac{2(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{(\sqrt{3} - 1)(\sqrt{3} + 1)} = \dfrac{2(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{3 - 1} = \sqrt{3} + 1$

Multiplying by the conjugate removes the surd from the denominator because $(\sqrt{3} - 1)(\sqrt{3} + 1) = 3 - 1 = 2$.
